draft.title: The gold rushes
card: Gold was found in New South Wales and Victoria in 1851. News spread fast, and a rush of diggers began.
Hundreds of thousands of people came to the colonies over the next years. Most came from Britain and Ireland, and many came from China.
The new people and the gold made the colonies larger and richer. Towns grew, and Victoria became the most populous colony.
Some European miners resented the Chinese miners, who worked hard and often stayed in groups. This hostility led to riots, such as those at Lambing Flat in 1861.
draft.remember: Gold brought people and wealth to the colonies, and hostility to Chinese miners led to riots.

a.q: Which of these was a result of the gold rushes in the 1850s?
opts: The population of the colonies grew quickly
The colonies lost most of their people overseas
Sheep farming ended across the colonies
The six colonies joined as one nation at once
a.why: Hundreds of thousands of migrants arrived, so the population rose sharply. Federation did not follow at once, as the colonies stayed separate until 1901.
a.clue: Think about who arrived after the news spread.

b.q: At Lambing Flat in 1861, crowds attacked Chinese miners on the goldfields. What best explains why this happened?
opts: Some European miners resented the Chinese miners
Chinese miners had refused to buy a mining licence
The colonial government had banned all mining
Chinese miners had found all the gold in the area
b.why: Hostility from some European miners towards Chinese miners led to riots. The other options are not reasons given for the riots, and the card does not say the Chinese miners broke any rule.
b.clue: Look at what the card says caused the riots.

a.best: The population of the colonies grew quickly

b.best: Some European miners resented the Chinese miners

problems.detail: The card explains the resentment only by saying Chinese miners 'worked hard and often stayed in groups'. It leaves out racial prejudice and competition for gold, the main causes historians give. Students could take away that the Chinese miners' own behaviour caused the hostility. Name racism and competition for gold as causes.

check.summary: The facts and both questions check out. The card's only reasons for European resentment are the Chinese miners' hard work and group living, with no mention of racism or competition. That could suggest the victims caused the hostility and should be reworded.

proposal.title: The gold rushes
card: Gold was found in New South Wales and Victoria in 1851. News spread fast, and a rush of diggers began.
Hundreds of thousands of people came to the colonies over the next years. Most came from Britain and Ireland, and many came from China.
The new people and the gold made the colonies larger and richer. Towns grew, and Victoria became the most populous colony.

Many European miners were hostile to Chinese miners because of racism (prejudice based on race) and competition for gold. This hostility led to riots, such as those at Lambing Flat in New South Wales in 1861.
proposal.remember: Gold brought people and wealth, while racism and competition for gold led to riots against Chinese miners.

a.q: Which of these was a result of the gold rushes in the 1850s?
opts: The population of the colonies grew quickly
The colonies lost most of their people overseas
Sheep farming ended across the colonies
The six colonies joined as one nation at once
a.why: Hundreds of thousands of migrants arrived, so the population rose sharply. Federation did not follow at once, as the colonies stayed separate until 1901.
a.clue: Think about who arrived after the news spread.

b.q: At Lambing Flat in 1861, crowds attacked Chinese miners on the goldfields. What best explains why this happened?
opts: Racism and competition for gold among the miners
Chinese miners had refused to buy a mining licence
The colonial government had ordered the attacks
Chinese miners had started the fighting at the site
b.why: The hostility came from European miners, driven by racism and by competition for gold. It is wrong to blame the Chinese miners' own actions: the cause lay in the prejudice and rivalry of those who attacked them.
b.clue: Think about the attitudes and aims of the European miners.
